title: Group Projects
summary: A team full-stack app built with shared version control. Kickoff is Mon Jan 4, 2027 (Judith's Workshop), the deadline is Wed Jan 13 and presentations are Thu Jan 14, the day before graduation. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Build and present a full-stack app as a team, sharing one codebase through branches and pull requests.
required: Build a team full-stack app with version control (syllabus: Group Projects). Deadline Jan 13; presentations Jan 14.

steps.title: Practice the feature-branch workflow
steps.detail: Teams work on separate branches and merge through pull requests. Pair with a classmate on a throwaway repo: each of you makes a branch, opens a PR, and reviews and merges the other's.
steps.code:
git switch -c feature/my-change
git add .
git commit -m "Add my change"
git push -u origin feature/my-change
gh pr create --fill
steps.doneWhen: You've opened, reviewed and merged at least one PR on a shared practice repo.

steps.title: Cause and fix a merge conflict on purpose
steps.detail: On the same practice repo, have both of you edit the same line on different branches, then merge. Fixing it calmly now saves a panic in week 15.
steps.doneWhen: You've resolved a conflict and `git status` shows a clean working tree.

steps.title: Bring what you learned from your personal project
steps.detail: Write down what worked in your personal project (Compose setup, auth, planning files) and what you'd skip. Ask in #eagle_questions how teams and ideas are chosen, so you know whether to bring a pitch.
steps.doneWhen: Your notes have a short "reuse / avoid" list and you know how teams are picked.

concepts.meaning: A branch for one change, kept off main until it's reviewed.
A GitHub request to merge a branch, where teammates review the code first.
Git can't combine two edits to the same lines, so a person picks the result.
A teammate reads your changes before they merge, to catch bugs and share knowledge.
